Q1: Methanesulfonic acid presents known hazards (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards (CMR), oral hazards (ORL), and dermal/eye hazards (SKN). It also has an expanded perspective (Tier 2) for both environmental (ENV) and inhalation (IHL) hazards, indicating potential concerns beyond GHS classifications. However, there are significant data deficiencies (Tier 4) regarding its endocrine disruption (EDC) and organ/systemic hazards (OGN), meaning a complete hazard assessment for these areas is not yet possible.
Q2: Methanesulfonic acid is not listed on any official lists of concern. Conversely, it has been verified and included on the SCIL Green Circle list, indicating that it is generally considered to be of low concern based on available experimental and modeled data.
Q3: Methanesulfonic acid is relatively well-characterized within our dataset of fracking and petrochemical materials, boasting 23,000 literature references, which is considerably higher than the median. Its precise molecular formula (CH4O3S) and 'Small Molecule' substance class further confirm its well-defined nature. Despite this, there are still some data gaps, specifically regarding endocrine disruption and organ/systemic hazards, as indicated by two Tier 4 classifications in its hazard profile.
